contents: # The feature flags of phil/feature-flags-bundle: see vendor/phil/feature-flags-bundle/doc/configuration.md for every
# option. As written here, the flags come from this file and every request has an empty context, so a flag with rules
# or an experiment is off for everyone.
# The resolver of the context a request is evaluated in. Implement
# Phil\FeatureFlagsBundle\Application\Flag\EvaluationContextResolver in src/ and remove this line to target tenants,
# The database store of active states and of the flags the admin creates. Generate the migration of its two tables
# The audited toggle, which needs a state store (the database store gives one) and two services of the application.
# The admin screens, which need the toggle; import their routes and put them behind the firewall.
# The flags of this file, by name: true or false, or a map with active, rules, experiment and metadata.
* Declare flags in <comment>config/packages/phil_feature_flags.yaml</>, then list them: <comment>php bin/console phil:feature-flags:list</>.
* To target tenants, projects or subjects, implement <comment>EvaluationContextResolver</> and remove <comment>context_resolver</> from the configuration.
* For the admin screens, enable <comment>doctrine</>, <comment>toggle</> and <comment>admin</>, create the tables with
<comment>php bin/console doctrine:migrations:diff</> then <comment>php bin/console doctrine:migrations:migrate</>, and import
<comment>@PhilFeatureFlagsBundle/config/routes/admin.php</> under a prefix that the firewall protects.
